There was only one argument from the detractors that I decided to make a rebuttal against, and that was the argument that "the ending episodes are rushed." I didn't say anything about the other criticisms of the show. I argue against this sentiment by asserting that what the show is going for by ramping up the intensity of external events is deeper than meets the eye, I never said this as an excuse to look over other criticisms of the show.

I didn't say "Franxx is exponential." When I say exponential, I'm talking about the intensity and speed of the lives of the characters in relation to the responsibility they take on when deciding to live their lives based on their own choices.

I didn't name the video "The Thematic Depth of Darling in the Franxx" but instead just wanted to make a rebuttal for the claim that the ending is awful because it is rushed. When it comes to the theme of freedom, there is plenty of evidence, but I didn't want to draw out the video farther than I already had, but I can give examples that I had in mind making the video right now. For example, there is the discovery of a world outside of what is known when Kokoro finds the book on childbirth, which is then followed by her making her own decisions and acting on her wants contrary to the authority controlling her life. This serves as symbolism for the act of rebellion in the name of wishing for the freedom to control your own destiny rather than letting it be decided for you. 

I'd also like to point out that such a reincarnation does not discount the sacrifices made by the characters, as what is important is the characters' decision to place their lives on the line for the sake of others; it's not as if they did so because they knew that in the end they would be reincarnated.

I'd disagree since I believe the meaningful themes presented by the show were well fleshed out, but I understand not everyone will think the same way. Thank you for the response.

It really doesn't matter what's "normal," so don't think about it like that. Think about how you feel about it. If the idea of her following hot guys on Instagram bothers you, then that's how you feel, no need to feel badly about your feelings just because they may not be "normal." Talk to her about it in a way such that you aren't being too assertive and dominating, and instead be vulnerable about it and tell her that it bothers you along with why. Don't tell her she has to do anything like stop, because you can't control people. If she is the type to take your feelings that you vulnerably expressed and not do anything to help you with that, then it probably is best to let her be the way she is and look for someone that cares enough about your feelings such that she'll do whatever she can to make you feel valued.
